question: The Union Ministry of Home Affairs in 2022 banned the Popular Front of India (PFI) and its associates for ______ years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is five.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Popular Front of India (PFI) and its associate/affiliate organisations were banned by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) in 2022 under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 (UAPA). (गैरकानूनी गतिविधियां (रोकथाम) अधिनियम)

 

• The ban was imposed for a period of five years, declaring PFI and its associates as an "unlawful association".

 

• The action followed nationwide raids and cases alleging PFI's links to terror funding and extremist activities.

 

• Several PFI-linked fronts — such as the Rehab India Foundation, Campus Front of India, and All India Imams Council — were banned simultaneously.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The UAPA, 1967 is India's principal anti-terror law, under which organisations can be declared "unlawful" and individuals can be declared "terrorists".

 

• The ban order was issued by the MHA and gazetted, making PFI's activities across India illegal for the notified period.

 

NOTE

 

• four (Option 2): Not the actual duration notified by the MHA for the PFI ban.

 

• seven (Option 3): Not the actual duration notified by the MHA for the PFI ban.

 

• two (Option 4): Not the actual duration notified by the MHA for the PFI ban.

question: Which of the following do/does NOT come under Union list of seventh schedule of the Indian constitution?
option_3: Audit of the accounts of the states
solution_text:
The correct answer is Intoxicating liquors.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution divides subjects into the Union List, State List and Concurrent List for legislative purposes between the Centre and the States. (सातवीं अनुसूची — संघ, राज्य व समवर्ती सूची)

 

• "Intoxicating liquors" — production, manufacture, possession, transport, purchase and sale — is Entry 8 of the State List (List II), meaning it is a subject on which only State legislatures can make laws.

 

• "Post and telegraphs, telephones, wireless, broadcasting" (Entry 31), "Audit of the accounts of the Union and of the States" (Entry 76), and "Banking" (Entry 45) are all subjects placed in the Union List (List I).

 

• Hence, among the given options, only Intoxicating liquors does NOT fall under the Union List.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Union List originally had 97 subjects (now 100 after the 101st and other amendments); the State List has 61 (originally 66); the Concurrent List has 52 (originally 47).

 

• Excise duty on alcoholic liquors for human consumption is also a State subject, reinforcing State control over the liquor trade.

 

NOTE

 

• Post and telegraphs (Option 2): A Union List subject (Entry 31), as communication networks of national importance are under central control.

 

• Audit of the accounts of the states (Option 3): A Union List subject (Entry 76), performed by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.

 

• Banking (Option 4): A Union List subject (Entry 45), reflecting central regulation of the banking sector through bodies like the RBI.

question: Which of the following indicates the correct limit of marginal propensity to consume (MPC)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 0 < MPC < 1.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Marginal Propensity to Consume (MPC) is defined as the ratio of the change in consumption to the change in income: MPC = ΔC / ΔY. (सीमांत उपभोग प्रवृत्ति)

 

• When income increases, a household normally spends part of the extra income and saves the rest, so 0 < MPC < 1 — consumption never falls when income rises (MPC is not negative) and consumption never rises by more than the entire increase in income (MPC is not greater than 1).

 

• A value of MPC close to 1 indicates that almost all extra income is spent, while a value close to 0 indicates that most of the extra income is saved.

 

• MPC is a key concept used in deriving the investment/expenditure multiplier (Multiplier = 1 / (1 − MPC)) in Keynesian economics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The counterpart of MPC is the Marginal Propensity to Save (MPS), and MPC + MPS = 1.

 

• Average Propensity to Consume (APC) = Total Consumption / Total Income, which is a different (though related) concept from MPC.

 

NOTE

 

• 0 < MPC < ∞ (Option 2): Incorrect upper bound; consumption cannot rise by more than the increase in income under normal theory, so MPC cannot be unbounded.

 

• -1 < MPC < 1 (Option 3): Incorrectly allows negative values; MPC is not negative under standard consumption theory.

 

• -1 < MPC < 0 (Option 4): Would imply consumption falls when income rises, which contradicts the basic psychological law of consumption.

question: Which of the following constellation is also called the hunter?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Orion.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Orion is one of the most conspicuous and well-known constellations in the night sky, named after a hunter in Greek mythology. (ओरायन तारामंडल — शिकारी)

 

• It is easily recognised by the three bright stars forming "Orion's Belt".

 

• Orion contains several bright stars, including Betelgeuse (a red supergiant) and Rigel (a blue supergiant).

 

• It is best visible in the night sky during winter months in the Northern Hemisphere.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Orion Nebula (M42), visible to the naked eye as a fuzzy patch below Orion's Belt, is a well-studied star-forming region.

 

• Orion is used as a guide to locate other stars/constellations, such as Sirius (the brightest star in the night sky) in Canis Major.

 

NOTE

 

• Cassiopeia (Option 1): A constellation named after a vain queen in Greek mythology; recognisable by its W/M-shaped pattern of five bright stars.

 

• Leo Major (Option 2): Represents a lion in Greek mythology, not a hunter.

 

• Ursa Major (Option 3): Known as the "Great Bear"; contains the well-known asterism the "Big Dipper" / "Saptarishi".

question: Kathak is the principal dance of which part of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Northern India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, and it is the principal classical dance of Northern India. (कथक — उत्तर भारत का शास्त्रीय नृत्य)

 

• The word "Kathak" is derived from "Katha", meaning story, and Kathakars were traditionally storytellers who narrated tales through dance, music and expressions.

 

• It evolved through temple and ritual narrations, and later flourished under the Mughal courts and the Nawabs of Awadh (Lucknow), developing intricate footwork, spins (chakkars) and expressive gestures.

 

• The three major gharanas (schools) of Kathak are Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras gharanas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Birju Maharaj was one of the most renowned exponents of the Lucknow gharana of Kathak.

 

• Kathak is distinct from Kathakali (Kerala), which is a different classical dance-drama form of Southern/Eastern-coastal India.

 

NOTE

 

• Eastern India (Option 2): Associated with classical dance forms such as Odissi (Odisha).

 

• North-Eastern India (Option 3): Known for dance forms such as Sattriya (Assam), not Kathak.

 

• Southern India (Option 4): Associated with classical forms such as Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu) and Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh).

question: Mohiniyattam belongs to ______ in India, takes its name from the celestial enchantress Mohini.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form belonging to Kerala, and is one of the eight classical dance forms of India. (मोहिनीअट्टम — केरल का शास्त्रीय नृत्य)

 

• Its name is derived from "Mohini", the enchantress avatar of Lord Vishnu, combined with "attam" meaning dance — hence "the dance of the enchantress".

 

• It is characterised by graceful, swaying body movements, gentle footwork, and expressive facial gestures (abhinaya), traditionally performed as a solo recital by women.

 

• The compositions are usually in Malayalam, and the dance draws thematic content from the Lasya style, emphasising the feminine, graceful elements of dance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kerala is also home to the classical dance-drama Kathakali and the martial art Kalaripayattu.

 

• Vallathol Narayana Menon, founder of the Kerala Kalamandalam, played a major role in reviving Mohiniyattam in the 20th century.

 

NOTE

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 2): Not associated with Mohiniyattam; known more for folk traditions and forms like Karma and Matki dance.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 3): Known for folk dance forms like Lavani, not for the classical dance Mohiniyattam.

 

• Odissa (Option 4): Home to the classical dance form Odissi, distinct from Mohiniyattam.

question: Which of the following is an exogenic force?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wind.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Geomorphic processes are classified into endogenic (internal) forces and exogenic (external) forces. (अंतर्जनित व बहिर्जनित बल)

 

• Exogenic forces originate from the atmosphere (outside the earth's surface) and constantly work to wear down (degrade) landforms — these include the action of wind, running water, glaciers and waves, causing weathering, erosion and deposition.

 

• Wind is a key exogenic agent, responsible for landforms like sand dunes, mushroom rocks and loess deposits, especially in arid and desert regions.

 

• Endogenic forces, by contrast, originate within the earth's crust/interior (due to heat energy) and tend to build up landforms — these include volcanism, earthquakes and diastrophic movements (folding, faulting).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Exogenic processes are broadly grouped as weathering, mass wasting (erosion) and deposition, all ultimately driven by gradation (levelling of the earth's surface).

 

• Endogenic energy largely comes from radioactivity, rotational and tidal friction, and primordial heat within the earth.

 

NOTE

 

• Landslides (Option 1): A form of mass wasting; in most standard classifications used for such questions it is grouped with rapid surface-degrading processes rather than being cited as the typical example of an exogenic force.

 

• Volcano (Option 3): Volcanism is an endogenic process, driven by magma and heat from within the earth's interior.

 

• Earthquake (Option 4): Earthquakes result from the release of internal tectonic stress and are classified as an endogenic force.

question: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding the Pacific Ocean?
option_1: The Pacific Ocean is perfectly oval in shape.
option_2: Asia, Australia, North and South Americas surround it
option_3: Mariana Trench, the deepest part of the earth, lies in the Pacific Ocean.
option_4: The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Pacific Ocean is perfectly oval in shape.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean in the world, covering about a third of the earth's surface. (प्रशांत महासागर — विश्व का सबसे बड़ा महासागर)

 

• Its shape is broadly triangular — wide near the Bering Strait/Arctic region in the north and narrowing towards Antarctica in the south — not oval, making this statement incorrect.

 

• It is surrounded by Asia and Australia to the west and North and South America to the east, which is a correct statement.

 

• It contains the Mariana Trench, the deepest point on earth (Challenger Deep, about 11 km deep), which is also a correct statement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Pacific Ocean is often divided by the equator into the North Pacific and South Pacific.

 

• The "Pacific Ring of Fire", a zone of intense volcanic and seismic activity, runs along the margins of the Pacific Ocean.

 

NOTE

 

• Asia, Australia, North and South Americas surround it (Option 2): This is a factually correct statement about the Pacific Ocean's bordering continents, so it is not the answer to a "NOT correct" question.

 

• Mariana Trench, the deepest part of the earth, lies in the Pacific Ocean (Option 3): This is factually correct; the Mariana Trench is indeed the deepest known part of the earth's oceans.

 

• The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean (Option 4): This is factually correct; the Pacific is the largest of all oceans by area and volume.

question: Jabalpur is located on the banks of which of the following rivers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narmada.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jabalpur, a major city in Madhya Pradesh, is situated on the banks of the Narmada River. (जबलपुर — नर्मदा नदी के तट पर)

 

• Near Jabalpur lies Bhedaghat, famous for its marble rocks (Marble Rocks Gorge) carved by the Narmada, and the spectacular Dhuandhar Falls.

 

• The Narmada rises from Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh and flows westward through Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Gujarat before draining into the Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea) — one of the few major Indian rivers flowing east to west.

 

• Jabalpur is an important administrative, industrial and cantonment city, and is sometimes called the "Marble City" of India due to the Bhedaghat marble rocks nearby.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Narmada forms the traditional boundary between North India and South (Deccan) India.

 

• Other notable towns/cities on the Narmada include Amarkantak, Hoshangabad (Narmadapuram), Bharuch, and it also flows near the Sardar Sarovar Dam.

 

NOTE

 

• Ganga (Option 1): Flows through northern Indian cities like Haridwar, Kanpur, Varanasi, and Patna — not Jabalpur.

 

• Godavari (Option 2): A major peninsular river flowing through Maharashtra, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh — not associated with Jabalpur.

 

• Chambal (Option 3): A tributary of the Yamuna, flowing through Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, but Jabalpur is not situated on it.

question: Who received the Vyas Samman for the novel "Patliputru Ki Samragi"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prof. Sharad Pagare.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Vyas Samman is a prestigious literary award instituted by the K.K. Birla Foundation, given annually for an outstanding literary work in Hindi published in the preceding ten years. (व्यास सम्मान — के.के. बिड़ला फाउंडेशन)

 

• Prof. Sharad Pagare received the Vyas Samman for his Hindi historical novel based on the Mauryan-era empress of Patliputra.

 

• Prof. Pagare is a noted Hindi litterateur from Madhya Pradesh, known for historical fiction rooted in ancient Indian history.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Vyas Samman carries a cash prize and is considered one of India's most prestigious literary honours, alongside the Saraswati Samman (also by the K.K. Birla Foundation, for works in any Indian language listed in the Eighth Schedule).

 

• Other notable Vyas Samman awardees over the years include Amarkant, Ramdarash Mishra, and Mridula Garg, among others.

 

NOTE

 

• Surendra Verma (Option 1): A Hindi playwright/novelist, but not the recipient of the Vyas Samman for this particular novel.

 

• Vishwanath Tripathi (Option 3): A noted Hindi critic and writer, but not the correct answer for this specific award and work.

 

• Dr. Sunita Jain (Option 4): A Hindi poet and novelist, but not the recipient of this particular Vyas Samman.

question: ______ won the (FIBA) Women’s Basketball World Cup 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is United States of America.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2022 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup was held in Sydney, Australia. (फीबा महिला बास्केटबॉल विश्व कप 2022)

 

• The United States of America won the tournament, defeating China in the final, continuing its dominant record in women's basketball.

 

• This continued the USA's long-standing dominance in the tournament, having won the title multiple times previously.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup is organised by the International Basketball Federation (FIBA) and is held every four years.

 

• China's strong run to the final of the 2022 edition was considered a notable achievement for Asian basketball.

 

NOTE

 

• India (Option 2): India did not win the 2022 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup; India is still building its presence in international basketball.

 

• Japan (Option 3): Japan did not win the 2022 edition, though Japan has been a competitive Asian team in women's basketball.

 

• China (Option 4): China was the runner-up (finalist), losing to the USA in the final, but did not win the title.

question: Which of the following shortcut key is used to move the cursor one word to the left in MS-Word 365?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ctrl + Left arrow key.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In MS-Word, the Ctrl + Left Arrow key shortcut moves the text cursor one word to the left. (माइक्रोसॉफ्ट वर्ड — शब्द के अनुसार कर्सर स्थानांतरण)

 

• Correspondingly, Ctrl + Right Arrow moves the cursor one word to the right.

 

• Adding Shift to these combinations (Ctrl + Shift + Left/Right Arrow) selects text word by word instead of just moving the cursor.

 

• These shortcuts work uniformly across modern versions of MS-Word, including MS-Word 365.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ctrl + Up/Down Arrow moves the cursor to the beginning of the previous/next paragraph.

 

• Home and End move the cursor to the beginning and end of the current line respectively, while Ctrl + Home/End moves to the beginning/end of the whole document.

 

NOTE

 

• Ctrl + PageUp (Option 1): Moves the cursor to the top of the previous page/screen, not one word to the left.

 

• Shift + Left arrow key (Option 3): Selects one character to the left (extends selection), it does not move by whole words.

 

• Shift + PageUp (Option 4): Selects text up to the previous page/screen, unrelated to moving by a single word.

question: Which of the following is a rare species as per International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Asiatic buffalo.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Species are broadly classified (as commonly taught in Indian school/competitive-exam geography, based on the IUCN's conservation categorisation) into groups such as Normal, Endangered, Vulnerable, Rare, Endemic and Extinct species. (दुर्लभ प्रजातियां — असम का जंगली भैंसा)

 

• "Rare species" are those with a small population which may become endangered or vulnerable if not protected/conserved in time.

 

• The Asiatic wild buffalo (Bubalus arnee) — found in parts of Assam, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Madhya Pradesh — is a classic example listed under this "Rare" category, along with animals like the Himalayan brown bear and desert fox.

 

• Other species listed under this classification, such as the lion-tailed macaque and Gangetic river dolphin, are typically categorised as Endangered, a more severe risk level than "Rare".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's wildlife protection framework broadly follows the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and various IUCN Red List categories (Least Concern, Near Threatened, Vulnerable, Endangered, Critically Endangered, Extinct).

 

• The Asiatic wild buffalo is the state animal of Chhattisgarh and is protected in reserves such as Udanti-Sitanadi (Chhattisgarh) and Kaziranga (Assam, for the related population).

 

NOTE

 

• Lion tailed macaque (Option 1): An endangered primate species endemic to the Western Ghats, categorised as Endangered rather than "Rare".

 

• Gangetic dolphin (Option 3): India's national aquatic animal, categorised as Endangered on the IUCN Red List due to habitat loss and pollution.

 

• Blue sheep (Option 4): Found in the high Himalayas (Ladakh, etc.), it is categorised as being of Least Concern, not "Rare" or threatened.

question: Which of the following was the capital of Pandyas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madurai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pandya dynasty, one of the three ancient Tamil ruling dynasties (along with the Cholas and Cheras), had Madurai as its capital. (मदुरै — पांड्य वंश की राजधानी)

 

• Madurai was a major centre of Tamil culture and learning, and is traditionally associated with the Sangam Age (the "third Sangam" is said to have been held at Madurai).

 

• The famous Meenakshi Amman Temple in Madurai, dedicated to Goddess Meenakshi (a form of Parvati) and Lord Sundareswarar (Shiva), reflects the city's long religious and cultural significance.

 

• Pandya kings were known for their patronage of Tamil literature, trade (including pearl fisheries) and temple architecture.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Greek and Roman accounts (e.g., by Megasthenes) also mention the Pandya kingdom, indicating its ancient trade links with the West.

 

• The Pandyas had a resurgence in the 13th century under rulers like Jatavarman Sundara Pandya, before eventually being overshadowed by the Delhi Sultanate's expansion into the south.

 

NOTE

 

• Kaveripattinam (Option 1): An ancient port city associated with the Chola dynasty, not the Pandyas.

 

• Aihole (Option 3): Associated with the Chalukyas of Badami, known for early experiments in temple architecture, not the Pandyas.

 

• Puhar (Option 4): Another name/site associated with Kaveripattinam, the Chola port city, not the Pandya capital.

question: Which of the following is not an asexual form of reproduction in plants?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pollination.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Asexual reproduction in plants produces new individuals without the fusion of gametes, and includes methods like spore formation, vegetative propagation, and budding. (अलैंगिक जनन — बीजाणु, कायिक प्रवर्धन, मुकुलन)

 

• Pollination, in contrast, is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a flower, which is a key step leading to fertilisation — the fusion of male and female gametes — making it part of sexual reproduction.

 

• Spore formation (e.g., in ferns, mosses) and vegetative propagation (e.g., through cuttings, tubers, rhizomes) allow new plants to grow from a single parent without gamete fusion.

 

• Budding (e.g., in yeast, and vegetatively in some plants) involves a new individual developing from an outgrowth (bud) of the parent organism.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common examples of vegetative propagation in plants include potato (tuber), ginger (rhizome), and sugarcane (stem cutting).

 

• Sexual reproduction in flowering plants involves pollination followed by fertilisation, producing seeds with genetic variation, unlike asexual reproduction which produces genetically identical clones.

 

NOTE

 

• Spore formation (Option 1): An asexual method of reproduction seen in ferns, mosses and fungi, where spores develop into new individuals directly.

 

• Vegetative propagation (Option 2): An asexual method where new plants grow from vegetative parts (roots, stems, leaves) of the parent plant.

 

• Budding (Option 3): An asexual method of reproduction where a new organism develops from a bud/outgrowth on the parent body.

question: What is the colour of the outer zone of completion combustion of a candle flame?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Blue.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A candle flame has three distinct zones, based on the extent of combustion of the wax vapour. (मोमबत्ती की लौ के तीन क्षेत्र)

 

• The outermost zone gets the maximum supply of oxygen from the air, resulting in complete combustion of the wax vapour — this zone burns with a non-luminous blue colour and is the hottest part of the flame.

 

• The middle zone has partial/incomplete combustion due to limited oxygen, producing unburnt carbon particles that glow, giving a luminous yellow colour — this is the zone typically used for testing substances with a flame test, being moderately hot.

 

• The innermost zone (blue-black/dark zone) near the wick contains unburnt wax vapour and is the coolest part of the flame, appearing dark/blackish.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• This zonal structure of a flame was famously studied and demonstrated by Michael Faraday in his lectures on "The Chemical History of a Candle".

 

• The blue outer zone principle is used in some burners (like a Bunsen burner with the air hole open) to get a hotter, cleaner flame for laboratory heating.

 

NOTE

 

• Yellow (Option 2): This is the colour of the middle, luminous zone of incomplete combustion, not the outer zone.

 

• Black (Option 3): This roughly describes the innermost, coolest zone containing unburnt wax vapour, not the outer zone.

 

• Orange (Option 4): Not a standard textbook description of any distinct zone of a candle flame; the outer zone is blue due to complete combustion.

question: According to the law of demand, the consumer’s demand for a good must be ______.
option_1: directly related to the supply of the good
option_2: inversely related to the price of the good
option_3: directly related to the price of the good
option_4: inversely related to the supply of the good
solution_text:
The correct answer is inversely related to the price of the good.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Law of Demand states that, other factors remaining constant (ceteris paribus), the quantity demanded of a good is inversely related to its price. (मांग का नियम — कीमत और मांग में विपरीत संबंध)

 

• That is, when the price of a good rises, the quantity demanded falls, and when the price falls, the quantity demanded rises.

 

• This inverse relationship is graphically represented by a downward-sloping demand curve.

 

• The law of demand describes the relationship between price and quantity demanded — it does not directly link demand to the supply of the good.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Exceptions to the law of demand include Giffen goods and Veblen goods, where demand may rise even as price rises.

 

• Demand is also influenced by other factors like income, prices of related (substitute/complementary) goods, and consumer preferences/tastes, held constant while stating the law of demand.

 

NOTE

 

• directly related to the supply of the good (Option 1): Confuses the law of demand with the concept of market equilibrium/law of supply; demand and supply are separate, interacting concepts.

 

• directly related to the price of the good (Option 3): This is the opposite of the actual (inverse) relationship stated by the law of demand.

 

• inversely related to the supply of the good (Option 4): The law of demand describes demand's relationship with price, not with supply.

question: Which of the following teams did NOT qualify for the playoffs of the 15th edition of Indian Premier League?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mumbai Indians.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 15th edition of the Indian Premier League (IPL 2022) playoffs featured Gujarat Titans, Lucknow Super Giants, Rajasthan Royals, and Royal Challengers Bangalore. (आईपीएल 2022 — 15वां संस्करण)

 

• Mumbai Indians had a poor season in IPL 2022, finishing at (or near) the bottom of the points table, and thus did not qualify for the playoffs.

 

• Gujarat Titans, led by Hardik Pandya in their debut season, went on to win the IPL 2022 title, defeating Rajasthan Royals in the final.

 

• This was a rare instance of a debutant franchise (Gujarat Titans) winning the IPL title in its very first season.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• IPL 2022 was the first edition to feature 10 teams, with the addition of two new franchises: Gujarat Titans and Lucknow Super Giants.

 

• Jos Buttler (Rajasthan Royals) won the Orange Cap (highest run-scorer) in IPL 2022.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajasthan Royals (Option 1): Qualified for the playoffs and reached the final of IPL 2022, losing to Gujarat Titans.

 

• Royal Challengers Bangalore (Option 3): Qualified for the playoffs (via the eliminator) in IPL 2022.

 

• Gujarat Titans (Option 4): Not only qualified for the playoffs but went on to win the IPL 2022 title in their debut season.

question: How many total medals did Haryana win in the fourth edition of Khelo India Youth Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 137.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 4th edition of the Khelo India Youth Games (KIYG) 2022 was hosted by Haryana (with venues including Panchkula). (खेलो इंडिया यूथ गेम्स — चौथा संस्करण)

 

• As host state, Haryana topped the medal tally, winning a total of 137 medals.

 

• This tally comprised 52 gold, 39 silver, and 46 bronze medals.

 

• The Khelo India Youth Games is a national-level multi-disciplinary grassroots sporting event aimed at unearthing young sporting talent across India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Khelo India scheme was launched by the Government of India (Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports) to build a strong sports culture and identify talent at the grassroots level.

 

• Maharashtra was among the other strong performers at KIYG 2022, finishing among the top states.

 

NOTE

 

• 123 (Option 1): Not the correct total medal count for Haryana at the 4th Khelo India Youth Games.

 

• 101 (Option 2): Not the correct total medal count for Haryana at the 4th Khelo India Youth Games.

 

• 115 (Option 4): Not the correct total medal count for Haryana at the 4th Khelo India Youth Games.

question: The first cotton textile mill in Ahmedabad was started in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1861.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first cotton textile mill in India was established in Bombay in 1854 by Cowasjee Nanabhoy Davar. (भारत की पहली सूती वस्त्र मिल — बॉम्बे, 1854)

 

• The first cotton textile mill in Ahmedabad, the "Ahmedabad Spinning and Weaving Company", was started in 1861 by Ranchhodlal Chhotalal, often regarded as the pioneer of Ahmedabad's textile industry.

 

• This laid the foundation for Ahmedabad's rise as a major textile hub, eventually earning it the nickname "Manchester of India" (or "Manchester of the East").

 

• The growth of the cotton textile industry in western India (Bombay and Ahmedabad) was driven by proximity to raw cotton-growing regions, access to a port, and available capital and labour.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• By the late 19th and early 20th centuries, Ahmedabad had emerged as one of India's leading centres of the cotton textile industry, alongside Bombay.

 

• Ranchhodlal Chhotalal is also remembered for civic contributions to Ahmedabad, including public health and municipal reforms.

 

NOTE

 

• 1854 (Option 1): This is the year the first cotton mill was set up in Bombay, not Ahmedabad.

 

• 1851 (Option 3): Not the correct year for Ahmedabad's first cotton mill.

 

• 1867 (Option 4): Not the correct year for Ahmedabad's first cotton mill.

question: What is the full form of URL?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uniform Resource Locator.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator. (यूआरएल — यूनिफॉर्म रिसोर्स लोकेटर)

 

• It is the address used to locate a resource (a web page, image, file, etc.) on the internet/World Wide Web.

 

• A typical URL includes components such as the protocol (e.g., http/https), domain name, and path to the specific resource.

 

• URLs are fundamental to how browsers locate and retrieve resources across the web.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A related term, URI (Uniform Resource Identifier), is a broader concept that includes URLs (which locate a resource) and URNs (which name a resource without necessarily locating it).

 

• The concept of the URL was introduced by Tim Berners-Lee, one of the inventors of the World Wide Web.

 

NOTE

 

• Union Resource Language (Option 2): Not the correct expansion; "Union" and "Language" are not part of the standard term.

 

• Union Resource Locator (Option 3): Incorrect; the correct first word is "Uniform", not "Union".

 

• Uniform Resource Language (Option 4): Incorrect; the correct last word is "Locator", not "Language".

question: Who is the implementing agency of “Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM)” ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is NHA.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) aims to create a seamless digital health ecosystem in India, providing every citizen with a unique digital health ID and interoperable health records. (आयुष्मान भारत डिजिटल मिशन — राष्ट्रीय स्वास्थ्य प्राधिकरण)

 

• The National Health Authority (NHA) is the implementing agency for ABDM.

 

• ABDM was launched nationwide on 27 September 2021 (having earlier been piloted as the National Digital Health Mission).

 

• Key components of ABDM include the ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) ID, Healthcare Professionals Registry, and Health Facility Registry.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The NHA is also the apex body implementing Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY), the world's largest government-funded health assurance scheme.

 

• ABDM operates under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

 

NOTE

 

• IMA (Option 1): The Indian Medical Association is a professional body/association of doctors, not the implementing agency of ABDM.

 

• AIIMS (Option 3): All India Institute of Medical Sciences is a premier medical institution/hospital, not the implementing agency of ABDM.

 

• NITI Aayog (Option 4): India's premier policy think tank, involved in broader policy planning but not the designated implementing agency of ABDM.

question: “Skilling of girls in non-traditional livelihood (NTL)” has been included in which flagship scheme?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Beti Bachao Beti Padao.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP), launched in 2015, is a flagship scheme of the Government of India aimed at addressing the declining child sex ratio and promoting the education and empowerment of the girl child. (बेटी बचाओ बेटी पढ़ाओ योजना)

 

• Under revised guidelines, the scheme was expanded to include new interventions such as "Skilling of girls in non-traditional livelihoods (NTL)", aimed at broadening career and livelihood options for girls beyond conventional/stereotyped occupations.

 

• Other additions under the revised BBBP guidelines include components like menstrual hygiene awareness for adolescent girls.

 

• BBBP is implemented jointly by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and Ministry of Education.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• BBBP's core objectives include preventing gender-biased sex-selective elimination, ensuring survival and protection of the girl child, and ensuring her education and participation.

 

• The scheme was launched from Panipat, Haryana, a district that historically had one of the worst child sex ratios in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Rashtriya Mahila Kosh (Option 1): A national credit fund for women set up to provide micro-credit to poor women, unrelated to skilling under the NTL component.

 

• POSHAN Abhiyaan (Option 2): India's flagship nutrition mission targeting stunting, undernutrition and anaemia, not the scheme under which NTL skilling was added.

 

• Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (Option 4): A maternity benefit scheme providing cash incentives to pregnant and lactating mothers, unrelated to the NTL skilling initiative.

question: Provisions as to disqualification on ground of defection are mentioned under which schedule of the Indian constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10th schedule.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Provisions relating to disqualification of members of Parliament and State Legislatures on grounds of defection are contained in the Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution. (दसवीं अनुसूची — दल-बदल विरोधी कानून)

 

• The Tenth Schedule, popularly known as the "Anti-Defection Law", was inserted by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985.

 

• It lays down the grounds on which a member can be disqualified for defection — such as voluntarily giving up party membership or voting against the party whip without prior permission.

 

• The 91st Amendment Act, 2003 further strengthened this law by removing the earlier provision that exempted a group defection of at least one-third of a party's legislators from disqualification.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The decision on questions of disqualification under the Tenth Schedule is taken by the Speaker/Chairman of the House concerned, subject to judicial review (as held in Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu, 1992).

 

• Other schedules with well-known content include the 9th Schedule (laws protected from judicial review), 11th Schedule (powers of Panchayats) and 12th Schedule (powers of Municipalities).

 

NOTE

 

• 12th schedule (Option 1): Deals with the powers, authority and responsibilities of Municipalities (added by the 74th Amendment), not defection.

 

• 11th schedule (Option 2): Deals with the powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats (added by the 73rd Amendment), not defection.

 

• 9th schedule (Option 4): Contains laws and regulations that were originally intended to be protected from judicial review, unrelated to defection.

question: Who has been elected as new Prime Minister of Pakistan in April 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shehbaz Sharif.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Shehbaz Sharif was elected as the Prime Minister of Pakistan on 11 April 2022. (शहबाज़ शरीफ — पाकिस्तान के प्रधानमंत्री, अप्रैल 2022)

 

• He took office after his predecessor, Imran Khan, was removed from power through a no-confidence motion passed in Pakistan's National Assembly.

 

• Shehbaz Sharif is the younger brother of Nawaz Sharif, a former Pakistani Prime Minister, and leads the Pakistan Muslim League (Nawaz) [PML(N)].

 

• His government was formed as the head of a coalition of opposition parties following the political crisis of early 2022.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Prior to becoming PM, Shehbaz Sharif served as the Chief Minister of Punjab province, Pakistan, for multiple terms.

 

• Pakistan subsequently held general elections in February 2024, after which Shehbaz Sharif returned as Prime Minister in a coalition government.

 

NOTE

 

• Nawaz Sharif (Option 1): A former Prime Minister of Pakistan (and Shehbaz Sharif's elder brother), but he was not the one elected PM in April 2022.

 

• Abbas Sharif (Option 2): Not a recognised holder of the office of Pakistan's Prime Minister; not a correct option.

 

• Imran Khan (Option 3): He was the sitting Prime Minister who was removed from office via the no-confidence vote in April 2022, and was thus replaced, not elected, at this time.
